g.text: Frame 1. The index is a slice of the address. The root holds the table
80386 fetch: linear = CS hidden base + EIP. A data access: linear = DS hidden base + offset.
bits 31-22
directory index
bits 21-12
page-table index
bits 11-0
offset in the page
CR3 = physical address of the directory. Entry address = CR3 + index x 4. This kernel writes CR3 = 0.
RV32 VA bits 31-22 VPN[1], 21-12 VPN[0], 11-0 offset. satp bits 21:0 are the root page number.
ARMv7 VA bits 31-20 level 1, 19-12 level 2, 11-0 offset. TTBR0 = physical address of level 1.
AArch64 VA bits 38-30 level 1, 29-21 level 2, 20-12 level 3, 11-0 offset.
TTBR0_EL1 = physical address of the root. T0SZ = 25, so the walk starts at level 1.
Frame 2. A task switch writes a new root. Red is the value just stored
80386 loads this from the new TSS
CR3 = physical address of the new directory
Segment registers and the bit split stay
schedule does not write CR3. switch_to is an ljmp
RV32 satp = new root
ARMv7 TTBR0 = new root
AArch64 TTBR0_EL1 = new root
The next walk uses this table
Frame 3. setup_paging in head.s fills these four tables
edi = 0, ecx = 1024 x 5. stosl clears 20KB at physical 0, the directory plus four tables.
directory 0
The first four entries are the table address plus 7. Linear bits 31-22 are 0, 1, 2, and 3.
The tables identity-map the first 16MB. Linear N and physical N are the same cell.
CR3 = 0
CR0.PG = 1
CR0.PE = 1
startup_32 at address 0 has already run. This stosl replaces those bytes with the directory.
